This is the classic Monty Hall problem. When you first pick door 1, there is a 1/3 probability you are right and a 2/3 probability the car is behind one of the other two doors (door 2 or door 3). 

The host's action is not random; they must open a door that contains a goat. By opening door 3, the host does not change the initial 1/3 probability that your choice is correct, but they concentrate the entire 2/3 probability of the "other doors" into the remaining closed door 2. Therefore, switching doubles your chances of winning the car from 1/3 to 2/3.
